Chapter Seven: Growing Through Seasons of Doubt and Dryness
Every journey of faith has moments that feel... well, barren. Maybe you know what I mean—those stretches when God seems silent, prayers go unanswered, and your spiritual life just feels flat. It’s unsettling, especially if you once felt really close to Christ.
When this happens, it’s so easy to wonder if something’s wrong, or if your faith just isn’t working anymore. But here’s something to remember: these dry seasons are actually a normal part of the spiritual journey. They come with their own sort of invitation—a chance to grow in ways we might not expect.
Picture someone who once felt alive in their faith, but now? They’re struggling. Praying feels hard, and the routines that used to inspire them just don’t bring comfort anymore. Doubts start to sneak in. And let’s be honest—most of us don’t talk about these times, even though almost everyone experiences them.
The temptation is to give up, to think, “Maybe this dryness will never end.” But here’s the thing: in these quiet, difficult seasons, something is happening deep down, even if you can’t see it right away. The roots of faith are growing, reaching down further than before.
I know someone who, feeling abandoned by God, kept showing up anyway. Sitting in silence. Reading Scripture, even when it felt empty. And you know what? Over time, a new kind of faith started to take shape—not built on feelings, but on trust.
It became clear that Christ’s presence isn’t about emotion or spiritual highs. He’s just as present in the silence as He is in the joyful moments. Some people get caught up chasing those mountaintop experiences, but the real invitation is to stay faithful, even when the path is dark.
It’s in these seasons that faith is refined. Your heart learns to rest in Christ’s steady, unchanging love.
Sometimes, that dryness is actually a sign that something new is being born—a deeper dependence, a greater humility, maybe even a more honest relationship with Christ. The old ways might not work anymore, but the call is to keep pressing on. Keep seeking. Trust that Christ is still at work, even when He feels hidden.
And here’s the beautiful part: sooner or later, that dry season gives way to fresh life. What you’ve learned in the dark becomes a source of strength—and compassion—for others who are struggling too.
So, if you’re walking through doubt or dryness, know this: it’s not a detour. It’s actually a necessary part of growing in communion with Christ, and you’re not alone on that path.
